newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. council demands release of Lima hostages.
newsitem.headline: U.N. council demands release of Lima hostages.

text.p: Security Council members on Thursday condemned the seizing of hundreds of hostages by "terrorist elements" at the residence of Japan's ambassador to Peru and appealed for their immediate release.
"This intolerable act constitutes also an assault against the international community as a whole," council President Francesco Paolo Fulci of Italy said.

He issued a statement on behalf of all 15 council members reacting to the seizure by leftist guerrillas late on Tuesday of more than 480 people, including diplomats, government officials and businessmen, attending a diplomatic reception.
The guerrillas, belonging to the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement, have demanded the release of between 400 and 500 jailed comrades.
Fulci said council members "vigorously condemn the occupation of the residence of the ambassador of Japan in Lima, Peru, and the taking of hostages by terrorist elements."

The statement said the council had "always and firmly condemned terrorist acts, whatever the circumstances, in the most unequivocal terms." Such acts violated basic principles of international law and of human rights, as well as being an attempt to jeopardise the democratic system and threaten peace and security, it added.

Council members expressed their solidarity with the governments of Peru and Japan as well as with the governments of all countries concerned, and "appeal for the immediate release of all officials, diplomats and all other persons being held hostage," Fulci said.
